we present an algorithm that maximizes spatial reuse of spectrum in wireless ad hoc network, while still maintaining fairness among multi-hop flows.

1) the spatial reuse of bandwidth in wireless ad hoc network is maximized when the resource allocation algorithm considers the entire end-to-end flow as a whole, instead of breaking it into multiple single-hop subflows for scheduling, and 2) our proposed end-to-end fair bandwidth allocation (EEFBA) algorithm is able to provide such end-to-end fairness, while still maximizing the spatial reuse of the bandwidth.

we propose a new fair bandwidth allocation scheme for multi-hop wireless ad hoc networks that is based on a novel concept of "fairness ratio" and is able to maximize spatial reuse and maintain fairness across flows.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the intra-flow correlation must be taken into account when scheduling flows in a wireless ad hoc network.
, when maximizing spatial reuse in wireless ad hoc network, it is important to consider the end-to-end perspective in multi-hop flows.

, in order to provide end-to-end fair bandwidth allocation, it may not always be appropriate to break a multi-hop flow into multiple singlehop flows for scheduling purposes; the intra-flow correlation among the upstream and downstream hops of a multi-hop flow should be taken into consideration when scheduling the flows.
